'''David Neil Payne''' (born 13 August 1944) is a British professor of [[photonics]] who is director of the Optoelectronics Research Centre at the [[University of Southampton]]. He has made several contributions in areas of [[optical fibre]] communications over the last fifty years and his work has affected telecommunications and laser technology. Payne’s work spans diverse areas of photonics, from telecommunications and optical sensors to nanophotonics and optical materials, including the introduction of the first optical fibre drawing tower in a university.

==Career==
Payne’s work in fibre fabrication in the 1970s resulted in many of the special fibres used today.<ref>S.B.Poole, J.E.Townsend, D.N.Payne, M.E.Fermann, G.J.Cowle, R.I.Laming, P.R.Morkel,  Characterisation of special fibres and fibre devices
IEEE Journal of Lightwave Technology Special Issue 1989 Vol.7(8) pp.1242-1255
</ref> He was part of the team at Southampton that invented the [[erbium-doped fibre amplifier]], a type of [[optical amplifier]].<ref>R. J. Mears, L. Reekie, I. M. Jauncey, and D. N. Payne, in Digest of Topical Meeting on Optical Fiber Communication (Optical Society of America, Washington, D.C., Jan 1987), Paper W12;  R. J. Mears, L. Reekie, S. B. Poole, and D. N. Payne, Electron. Lett. 22,159 (Sept 1986)</ref> Although the idea was conceived and performed by [[Robert J. Mears|Robert Mears]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mears|first1=R.J.|last2=Reekie|first2=L.|last3=Poole|first3=S.B.|last4=Payne|first4=D.N.|date=1986|title=Low-threshold tunable CW and Q-switched fibre laser operating at 1.55 μm|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1049/el:19860111|journal=Electronics Letters|volume=22|issue=3|pages=159|doi=10.1049/el:19860111|bibcode=1986ElL....22..159M|issn=0013-5194|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mears|first1=R.J.|last2=Reekie|first2=L.|last3=Jauncey|first3=I.M.|last4=Payne|first4=D.N.|date=1987|title=Low-noise erbium-doped fibre amplifier operating at 1.54μm|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1049/el:19870719|journal=Electronics Letters|volume=23|issue=19|pages=1026|doi=10.1049/el:19870719|bibcode=1987ElL....23.1026M|issn=0013-5194|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The idea was adopted at Bell Laboratories in New Jersey, USA <ref>E. Desurvire, J.R. Simpson and P.C. Becker, High-gain erbium-doped traveling-wave fiber amplifier, Optics letters, Vol. 12, No. 11, November 1987</ref> and the two teams between them developed much of the EDFA technology we know today. The EDFA was a crucial component that fuelled the rapid growth in the internet through its ability to transmit and amplify large amounts of data.

Payne also pioneered [[fibre laser]]s and led the teams that invented the [[Single-mode optical fiber|single mode]] silica fibre laser and amplifier <ref>R.J.Mears, L.Reekie, S.B.Poole, D.N.Payne, Neodymium-doped silica single-mode fibre lasers, Electronics Letters 1985 Vol.21 (17) pp.738-740</ref> and broke the kilowatt barrier for the output of a fibre laser.<ref>Y.Jeong, J.K.Sahu, S.Baek, C.Alegria, D.B.S.Soh, C.Codemard, V.Philippov, D.J.Richardson, D.N.Payne, J.Nilsson, Ytterbium-doped double-clad large-core fibre lasers with kW-level continuous-wave output power, CLEO/IQEC 2004 San Francisco 16–21 May 2004 CMS</ref> Since then he has made discoveries which have contributed to the growth of fibre lasers for use in manufacturing and defence.

Payne is the current director of the Optoelectronics Research Centre at the [[University of Southampton]], one of the world’s largest research groups dedicated to photonics. He also directs the [[Photonics Hyperhighway]] research project, aimed at making internet connections 100 times faster.<ref>[http://www.orc.soton.ac.uk/655.html Pioneering research aims to make the internet faster] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161021064029/http://www.orc.soton.ac.uk/655.html |date=2016-10-21 }}, University of Southampton Optoelectronics Research Centre, 2011-01-28, with two audio recordings of Payne</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
He has received the UK Rank Prize for Optics, the  US [[Tyndall Award]] (1991) and the [[The Franklin Institute Awards|Benjamin Franklin Medal for Engineering]] (1998). He is also an [[Eduard Rhein Foundation]] Laureate (Germany). In 2001, Payne was awarded the [[Mountbatten Medal]] of the IEE (2001) and the Kelvin Medal of the eight major engineering institutions for distinction in the application of science to engineering (2004). The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) awarded him the  2007 Photonics Award for outstanding achievements in photonics, the first awarded outside the USA. In 2008, he won the $100,000 Marconi Prize for his work in developing the erbium-doped optical fibre amplifier. In 2011, the Marconi Society elected him Chairman.<ref>David N. Payne Elected Chairman of the Marconi Society, http://marconisociety.org/press/payneelected.html {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325013701/http://www.marconisociety.org/press/payneelected.html |date=2016-03-25 }}</ref> He was appointed a [[Fellow]]<ref name="RAE_fellows">{{cite web|title=List of Fellows|url=http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows|access-date=23 October 2014|archive-date=8 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160608094405/http://www.raeng.org.uk/about-us/people-council-committees/the-fellowship/list-of-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]] in 2005. In 2007, he was elected to the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] as one of only 240 foreign members.<ref>A GOLDEN 
TOUCH: PROFESSOR DAVID PAYNE CBE FREng FRS,  http://www.ingenia.org.uk/ingenia/issues/issue38/issue38_profile.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924035240/http://www.ingenia.org.uk/ingenia/issues/issue38/Issue38_Profile.pdf |date=2015-09-24 }}</ref> Payne was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2013 New Year Honours]] for services to photonics research and applications.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=60367 |date=29 December 2012 |page=1 |supp=y }}</ref> 

In 2022, Payne was awarded the [[VinFuture Prize|VinFuture Grand Prize]], valued at US $3 million shared with 4 others, for his development of optical fiber communication over five decades related to fiber design, optical amplifiers, specialty fibers, and high-powered lasers and amplifiers that made Internet transmission possible on a global scale, thanks to the ability to boost high-speed optical signals repeatedly.<ref>{{cite news |title=Winners of the Second Ever VinFuture Prize Awards Unveiled |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/winners-of-the-second-ever-vinfuture-prize-awards-unveiled-301707367.html |access-date=21 December 2022 |work=VinFuture Foundation |agency=Cision PR Newswire |publisher=Cision US Inc. |date=20 December 2022}}</ref>
